evidence.summary: Serial wall-time observations use time.monotonic around capture and selector invocation, with lookup/write boundaries replaced in the synthetic benchmark. Six chosen cases (decision, correction, lookup, exclusion, unfinished work, courtesy), two per baseline/current and Haiku model; all passed. Baseline current model all-case median 3.874s; Haiku 7.303s. Courtesy baseline 3.481–3.530s; exact shortcut 0.413–0.467ms in low-effort comparison and 0.674ms final. The target is zero selection for confirmed courtesy/unchanged dialogue while preserving corrections/checkpoints. Final six-case run passed on final prompt. Low effort gave no consistent advantage; no production model/effort change. Real relevance selector passed paraphrase, unrelated and injected instructions twice (3.15–7.17s); real checkpoint cases passed partial/full completion and no reopening, bodies 408/472 bytes. Every attempted case and failure is reported; successful results are not sampled from fastest runs. Bounds are synthetic chosen scenarios, not production distribution or a general latency SLO. Timing instrumentation has no nested profiler; its exact overhead and internal CPU/network decomposition were not measured. CLI version startup 6.7–10ms is a lower-bound probe only. No persistent selector/cache was introduced.

evidence.summary: Five ordered commits implement semantic features and supporting tests/docs. The capture shortcut only removes selector calls for exact courtesy pairs after a confirmed prefix (or entire courtesy dialogue); substantive capture still selects. Atomic hashed conversation controls persist binding/status/digest with no raw spool. One profile command plugin owns commands; provider instances own/dispose hooks. Retry uses the live pending snapshot or at most 64 active native history rows with exact digest match. Semantic fallback makes at most one search, one pull and one 8-second relevance selection; combined delivered context stays 12000 bytes and failures retain no unverified optional candidate. Checkpoints are complete replacements under 3000 bytes; completion only revises a supplied topic. Shared-model helper extraction is structural supporting reuse. No daemon, model change, new generic adapter interface, database migration or broad memory rewrite was introduced. Leave-all-unchanged misses the authorized features; retaining the current model avoids unsupported quality/performance tradeoffs. Larger persistence/concurrency designs add lifecycle costs without measured benefit. Reopen if native Hermes contracts change, misses recur or representative latency warrants a different selector.

Native model responses and Slack outbound transport are substituted in fixtures. Separate real-model checks cover only the named synthetic inputs; actual external Slack delivery and sustained task usefulness are unmeasured.
Selection/relevance are fallible. Multi-note writes are not atomic; abrupt death can lose pending text. Cold retry refuses missing, changed or compacted original history.
Fallback adds one bounded relevance-model call after a lexical miss; typical-turn latency and long-term control-file retention were not measured.
